P143 requires and guards a downstream mainline-convergence outcome in the plan, but P07 owns execution and default-branch integration. This preserves global capability coverage without giving P143 primary execution ownership.

P143 must persist a durable convergence plan artifact with dispositions, evidence states, and successor handoff so later sessions resume without reconstruction; plan durability is load-bearing for the P55/P07 sequence.
P143 records donor floors and pinned donor identity as provenance inputs to C without claiming global primary ownership of provenance.
P143 plans phases and the first vertical slice in isolation from donor mutation and from P55 creation, keeping planning a non-mutating lane.
P143 guards orthogonal destination proposal, provider, and authority states. AVAILABLE, EXISTS_OWNED, and execution authorization remain mechanically distinct; provider truth cannot mint permission.
P143 advertises a distinct prompt identity and routes convergence terms to itself while routing simple bootstrap to P55 without absorbing those identities.
P143 does not execute implementation; it is aware of and routes creation to P55 and post-create convergence to P07.
Recurring process hardening remains owned elsewhere; P143 only surfaces recurrence risks discovered during dispositioning.
P114 requires current scoped evidence before reusing freshness-bounded repository/provider context while leaving the underlying evidence owners authoritative.
P114 uses query-issued temporal provenance and targeted refresh to prevent stale proof from being silently promoted across later turns.
P114 fails closed on unknown profile, network, execution, account, and material provider state instead of inventing execution truth.
P114's repeated-drift handoff preserves the first executable next action without taking ownership of the resumed implementation.
P114 observes context and routes resumed execution; it does not own repository implementation.
Repeated Canary or artifact-handoff failures route to P13/P94; P114 does not absorb recurrence ownership.
